- [2023/05/26] The user inquired about the GDPR and its relation to data locality.
- [2023/05/26] The GDPR took effect in the EU on May 25, 2018.
- [2023/05/26] The GDPR applies to organizations within the EU/EEA and those outside if they offer goods/services to or monitor individuals in the EU/EEA.
- [2023/05/26] Key GDPR principles include lawfulness, fairness, transparency, purpose limitation, data minimization, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity, confidentiality, and accountability.
- [2023/05/26] The GDPR grants rights such as access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, and data portability to individuals.
- [2023/05/26] Non-compliance with the GDPR can result in fines up to €20 million or 4% of global annual turnover.
- [2023/05/26] The GDPR does not explicitly mention "data locality" but addresses cross-border data transfer and storage.
- [2023/05/26] Chapter V of the GDPR outlines provisions for data transfers to third countries or international organizations.
- [2023/05/26] Data transfers outside the EU/EEA require adequate protection, which can be ensured through SCCs, BCRs, or codes of conduct/certification mechanisms.
- [2023/05/26] The GDPR's requirements for cross-border data transfers can encourage local data storage and processing to ensure compliance.
